correctness.rationale: The independent-parent construction makes each leaf indicator Y_j have P(Y_j)= (j-1)/(n-1). Conditioning on the attachment of arrival k>max(i,j) to i yields positive cross-tag covariance (j-1)/[(n-1)(k-1)(k-2)]; the missing self-term is exactly -((i-1)/(n-1))(H_{n-1}-H_{i-1}). Summing all j != i yields the displayed polynomial part; the early n=7 boundary and terminal n zero follow. After factoring (n-i)/(n-1), the harmonic ratio t/(N-t)*sum_{r=t+1}^N1/r strictly increases with t, yielding at most one sign transition and the unique scaling root f(x)=(1-x)/2-x log(1/x). Fresh exhaustive independent parent-array enumeration for n=3..8 corroborated all 27 tagged covariance values, not used as an infinite proof.

originality.rationale: Earlier root degree/leaf-covariance records show a positive root quantity but do not imply nonroot behavior because a tagged nonroot vertex can itself be a leaf, yielding the decisive negative self-leaf term. Janson treats the asymptotic joint distribution of aggregate degree counts, not covariance of one prescribed birth label with the global leaf count. Hartle-Krapivsky studies age-stratified leaf degree and total leaf count separately; those are not this tagged joint mixed moment nor its monotone birth-time sign boundary.

value.rationale: A specified vertex birth time and total leaves are natural local/global statistics of the classic random recursive tree. The exact covariance formula and uniquely age-ordered sign transition with nontrivial limiting fraction explain competition between self-exclusion and beneficial attachments, a structural result beyond a routine marginal moment.

final_claim: For uniform random recursive tree n>=3 and nonroot vertex label 2<=i<=n, exact covariance of child count and global leaves is ((n-i)(n-3))/(2(n-1)^2)-((i-1)/(n-1))(H_{n-1}-H_{i-1}); signs in nonterminal labels are strictly one-crossing and first positive at n=7, with limiting birth fraction x*=0.2846681370... . Terminal label n has zero covariance.
